stories.headline: Houthi missile strike on Riyadh airport kills 12 and injures hundreds
stories.body:
Houthi forces struck King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with a missile on Saturday [c1]. At least 12 people died in the attack [c1]. Over 300 people suffered injuries at the airport [c1]. Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation reported that 309 people were injured [c3]. The aviation authority said some of the injured are in critical condition [c3].

Four Saudi citizens and two Bangladeshis died in the strike [c2]. Citizens from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine, and Sudan were also killed [c2]. An unnamed regional official said a missile hit a terminal complex [c14]. The complex houses terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights [c14]. Regional officials said earlier Houthi attacks on the airport on Thursday damaged three planes [c16].

Flight operations at the Riyadh airport were temporarily stopped after the attack [c5]. Planes flying to Riyadh were sent to other airports [c5]. FlightAware reported that at least 225 flights were cancelled over 24 hours [c6]. The US and UK embassies in Riyadh warned their citizens to stay away [c7]. They told citizens to avoid the airport and the surrounding area [c7].

Another strike occurred in eastern Saudi Arabia [c8]. A military coalition fighting the Houthis said a projectile fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam [c8].

The Houthis warned airline companies to stop flying in Saudi airspace [c12]. They said any plane in Saudi airspace except over Mecca and Medina is a target [c12]. The Houthis also warned Pakistan against fighting them for Saudi Arabia [c13]. They said they would treat Pakistan like Saudi Arabia if Pakistan gets involved [c13].

US President Donald Trump spoke to reporters at the White House [c11]. Reporters asked if the United States would join strikes against the Houthis [c11]. Trump said he will make a decision soon [c11]. Regional officials told the AP last month that Saudi Arabia was running low on missile interceptors [c15]. Saudi Arabia asked France, Britain, Pakistan, and Egypt for air defense help [c15].

Earlier strikes hit King Khalid International Airport and Abha International Airport on October 6 and 7 [c4]. The aviation authority said those earlier attacks killed three people [c4]. Those attacks also injured 36 people [c4].

In Yemen, pro-government forces secured the port of Mokha [c9]. Mokha sits on the Bab al-Mandab Strait near the Red Sea [c9]. Spokesman Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili gave details about the fighting [c10]. He said government forces killed at least 1,150 Houthis in operation 'Dawn of Yemen' [c10]. Forces completed almost 2,000 targeted operations during that mission [c10].

vocab.meaning: an object shot or thrown through the air as a weapon
missiles used to shoot down incoming enemy missiles

stories.headline: Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia kills 20 as Trump demands new leadership in Ukraine
stories.body:
Russian forces attacked the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia with five glide bombs on Saturday [c17]. The attack killed at least 20 people, including four children [c17]. At least 32 other people were injured in the bombing [c17].

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke about the attack [c18]. He said Russia was saying thanks for a US deal easing sanctions on Russian diesel exports [c18]. US President Donald Trump said Russia agreed to supply over 300,000 tonnes of diesel right away [c26]. Russia will supply 500,000 tonnes in November and millions more later [c26].

Trump said Ukraine needs a new leader who can make a deal [c20]. He said Zelensky has not done enough to end the war [c20]. Trump claimed Ukraine lost 30 percent of its land and 2 million people under Zelensky [c24]. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga defended Zelensky [c25]. Sybiga said Zelensky has the support of the Ukrainian people [c25].

In other attacks, a Russian missile hit a restaurant in Kyiv and wounded seven people [c27]. Russia said its drones struck a Kyiv data center and a ship carrying military supplies [c28]. Ukrainian attacks killed four civilians in Russian-occupied Luhansk [c22].

vocab.meaning: penalties imposed on a country to limit its trade
people killed or injured in a war or accident

stories.headline: Hurricane Isaias weakens after killing four people and causing power outages
stories.body:
Hurricane Isaias made landfall on Florida's panhandle as a category 2 storm late Friday [c30]. It weakened to a post-tropical cyclone on Saturday [c30]. The storm produced winds of 105 mph [c36].

At least four people died during the storm [c31]. Two deaths occurred in Escambia County, Florida, and two in Alabama [c31]. Trees fell on homes and killed two people [c32]. One person in Escambia County died from generator gas poisoning [c33]. Four family members went to the hospital [c33].

Nearly 550,000 customers had no power across Florida, Alabama, and Georgia on Saturday afternoon [c35]. Outages peaked earlier at over 900,000 [c35]. The storm blew off a hotel roof in Pensacola and flattened a boathouse in Destin [c34]. It also damaged a high-rise building in Panama City Beach [c34].

US President Donald Trump approved emergency help for Florida, Alabama, and Georgia [c43]. The US Department of Energy released 4 million barrels of crude oil due to supply disruptions [c44].

vocab.meaning: the arrival of a storm over land
disturbances that stop a process or event

stories.headline: Delhi Police detain thousands to stop anti-CEC protest
stories.body:
Delhi Police conducted large-scale detentions on October 10 to stop a youth protest [c52]. Protesters demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over deleted voter lists [c52]. Police enforced Section 163 prohibitory orders in New Delhi district [c53]. Senior police officers said nearly 3,000 people were detained across Delhi [c58].

Authorities closed gates at 45 Delhi Metro stations [c63]. They cancelled more than 250 trains [c63]. Officials suspended mobile internet in central Delhi [c63]. Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan approved internet cuts near eight temporary jail sites [c65]. The Delhi government converted four sports stadiums into temporary jails [c66]. The Supreme Court said on Friday that authorities cannot use a sledgehammer to kill a fly [c64].

Police detained several political leaders [c62]. AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal was detained while leaving his house [c62]. Former Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee was detained at a bus stop with several lawmakers [c60]. Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and former Tripura chief minister Manik Sarkar were also detained [c61].

Officers detained CJP representatives Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and Ashutosh Ranka after they boarded a flight [c54]. Police detained YouTuber Dhruv Rathee at a flat in Gurugram [c55]. Advocate Nipun Saxena said detaining CJP members outside order zones was illegal [c56]. Former Supreme Court judge Abhay S. Oka said authorities must give reasons for restraint quickly [c57].

BJP leaders strongly criticized the protest [c46]. BJP president Nitin Nabin alleged two groups worked with foreign forces to hurt India [c46]. BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra called the protest a flop show [c51]. Patra called Congress leader Rahul Gandhi Mir Jafar [c51]. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta accused Gandhi and Kejriwal of creating trouble [c59].

Congress supported the youth but did not join the street protests [c47]. Rahul Gandhi spoke at an event in Chennai [c50]. He praised the students and called top officials villains [c48].

vocab.meaning: used to forbid or stop certain actions
held in official custody or prevented from leaving

stories.headline: Fresh ethnic violence in Manipur leaves nine people dead
stories.body:
Clashes and village attacks killed at least five people in Manipur's Kamjong and Ukhrul districts [c67]. The violence started on Friday evening [c67]. Former Manipur Chief Minister Nongthombam Biren Singh said seven people died in 24 hours [c68]. Scroll.in reported that nine people died between Friday and Saturday [c75].

A 42-year-old Kuki woman named Domkhonei Touthang was shot dead in Chassad Kuki village [c69]. The Kuki Students' Organisation blamed security forces for her death [c73]. Gunfights killed a 22-year-old man named Michael Ngamminlen Haokip on Saturday morning [c70]. A 40-year-old Gurkha farmer named Sandeep Rai was shot dead while driving [c71].

Attackers burned at least 14 homes in Kamjong district [c79]. Around Chassad, 10 houses and 20 shops burned down [c82]. The Tangkhul Naga Long committee alleged Kuki extremists killed two Naga civilians [c72]. Four Naga volunteers died in separate attacks [c76]. One guard was reportedly beheaded in a video [c80].

Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi [c74]. District officials imposed emergency movement restrictions in parts of Kamjong district [c81].

vocab.meaning: relating to a group of people with a shared culture or background
people who hold radical opinions and may use violence
